MDCCCXXVIII.

PREFACE.

THE INDEX now printed was compiled by the late Mr. Raithby, in pursuance of an Order made at a Board of the Commissioners on Public Records, dated 29 June 1816, which directed that a General Index to the Statutes of the Realm should be framed, in Two Parts; One Alphabetical, the other Chronological; the former including the several Matters contained in the Statutes, in Alphabetical Arrangement, in a Manner indicating only the Subject Matter of each Clause, and not professing to give the Substance of the Enactment; the latter including the several Matters contained in the Statutes under each Head succinctly, and giving the Substance of their respective Enactments, proceeding under each Head chronologically.

The Alphabetical Index was published in 1824, and it was then stated in the Preface, that at that Time considerable Progress had been made in the General Chronological Index.

Mr. Raithby proceeded with much Assiduity in the Compilation of the present Volume, until Christmas 1824, when, being attacked with severe Indisposition, his Progress was retarded, his Labours, however, never being discontinued, but carried on uninterruptedly, with all the Attention which Circumstances would permit, until his Death in August 1826, at which Time the Volume had been altogether compiled in MS. and printed as far as Page 569.

Upon Mr. Raithby’s Decease, the Task of correcting the Press devolved on his Clerk Mr. Elliot, (who had throughout the whole been employed by him on both Indexes,) under the immediate Care and Superintendence of the Secretary, and by them the present Volume has been made complete.

JOHN CALEY, Secretary.

WILLIAM ELLIOT.

Remedies for Usurpations of Advowsons. - -

After the respective Deaths of Ancestor, Tenant by the Curtesy, for Years, Life, or in Tail, it shall be in the Election of the Party disturbed whether he will sue a Writ of Quare impedir, or of Darrien Presentment, and he shall have his Damages in such Writs. So Writs shall be granted for Advowsons of Chappies, Prebends, Vicarages, Hospitals, Abbeys, Priories, and other Houses. When an Ad-vowson descends to Parceners, though one present Twice and usurps upon his Coheir, yet he that was negligent shall not be barred, but shall have his Turn. So as to Presentations to Churches of Femes Covert, and of Religious Persons.

For restoring Advowsons, Rectories, Impropriate Glebe Lands, and Tithes, to the King’s Subjects, and making void certain Charges imposed for Delinquency by the late usurped Powers.

the King’s Subjects Merchant Denizens of the same Realm grievously impoverished, and great Treasure by the same Aliens brought out of this Realm, and the Navy of the said Realm greatly destroyed and hindered. 18 Hen. FI. c. 4.

Aliens shall not sell any Merchandizes to Aliens •, on Pain of Forfeiture of the same Merchandises. - Ib.

Merchant Aliens shall be under the Survey of Hosts assigned by the Mayors, Sheriffs, or Bailiffs of Cities,

Towns, Boroughs, or Ports. - Ib.

Hosts shall be privy to all Sales and Contracts by Aliens. - Ib.

Aliens shall sell their Merchandizes, except Cloths of Gold, &c. within Eight Months, or shall sell them for Money, and with the same Money they shall buy within the Time aforesaid other Merchandizes growing and made within the said Realm, upon Pain to forfeit all the said Money within the said Term not so employed. - Ib.

Foreign Goods not so sold may be exported Custom free. - Ib.

The Hosts shall register all Contracts, and send a Transcript into the Exchequer two Times by the Year ; and the said Host shall take for his

Labour Two-pence for every Twenty

Shillings in Value. - Ib.

The Hosts shall be sworn. - Ib.

They may be displaced for Misconduct, and moreover be punished after his deserving by Discretion of the same Mayors, Sheriffs, and Bailiffs. -

Aliens not submitting to these Regulations shall be imprisoned until sufficient Surety found.

And if any such Mayor, Sheriff, or Bailiff let any such Merchant willingly to be without Host in the Form aforesaid, and go at large, without punishing in the Form aforesaid, the same Mayor, Sheriff, or Bailiff shall forfeit Twenty Pounds to the King. -

Persons refusing to be Hosts shall pay every Time to the King Ten Pounds. - - -

Provided always, That the Merchants of the Hanse of Almaine, and all other Merchants under the King’s Obedience, be not comprised within this Act. -

This Act repealed, as therein mentioned, 3 Geo. IV. c. 41. §1.

Captures of Ships not having Safe Conducts on board or inrolled in Chancery, declared valid.

Proclamations of this Act to be made upon the Sea Coasts incontinently after this Ordinance.

This Act repealed, as therein mentioned, 3 Geo. Iff. c. 41. §1.

Touching the Merchants of Italy. This Act repealed, as therein mentioned, 3 Geo. IF. c. 41. §2. Recital of the Grievances done by Italian and other Merchant Strangers, to the King and his Realm, by importing and selling their Goods by Retail. - - -

Italian Merchants shall sell their Wares already imported, &c. in Gross, and employ their Money in Commodities of this Realm, upon Pain of Forfeiture of the Value, as well of all the said Wares and Merchandizes kept and not sold before the said First Day of May, or otherwise sold than is before rehearsed, as of so much Money as so shall be made over by Exchange contrary to this Act. - -

They shall sell their Wares in future within Eight Months, and employ their Money in Commodities of this Realm. - - -

Two Months allowed to them after the Eight Months, to carry away the Wares remaining unsold.

The Merchants may remove their Goods from one Port to another.

On the Apparel of Servants. - -Servants. — Recital of the outrageous and excessive Apparel of divers People against their Estate and Degree, to the great Destruction and Impoverishment of all the Land.

Grooms, as well Servants of Lords as of Mysterys, and that have Cloths for their Vesture or Hosing, whereof the whole Cloth shall not exceed Two Marks, and their Wives and Children of the same Condition, and they shall wear no Veils passing I2d. a Veil. -Of the Apparel of Tradesmen, Artificers, and Yeomen, and of their Wives and Children.

Handicraftsmen and Yeomen. — People of H andicraft and Yeomen shall not wear Cloth of an higher Price for their Vesture or Hosiery than within 40s. the Cloth, nor Stone, nor Cloth of Silk, nor of Silver, nor Girdle, Knife, Button, Ring, Garter, nor Owche, Ribband, Chain, nor no such other Things of Gold or Silver, nor no Manner of Apparel embroidered, aimeled, nor of Silk, and that their Wives and Children be of the same Condition, and that they wear no Veil but of Yarn made within the Realm, nor no manner of Fur, nor of Budge, but only Lamb, Coney, Cat, and Fox.

Of the Apparel of Gentlemen under the Estate of Knights not having Land or Rent of j^ioo per Annum, and of Esquires of ^200 per Annum, and of their Wives and Children.

Esquires and Gentlemen under the Estate of a Knight, which have no Land nor Rent to the Value of ^100 a Year, shall not wear Cloth of an higher Price than within Four Marks and a Half the whole Cloth, and that their Wives and Children be of the same Condition.

Esquires which have Land or Rent to the Value of 200 Marks by the Year and above, may wear Cloths of the Price of Five Marks the whole Cloth, and other Apparel reasonably garnished of Silver, and that their Wives and Children, may wear Fur.

Former Acts of Apparel repealed. Ib.

Recital of the Necessity of repressing the inordinate Increase daily more and more used in the sumptuous and costly Array and Apparel worn in this Realm, to the manifest and notorious Detriment of the Common Weal, the Subversion of good and politic Order, and Distinction of People according to their Estates, Dignities, and Degrees, and to the utter Impoverishment and Undoing of inexpert and light Persons inclined to Pride, the Mother of all Vices. - Ib.

This Act repealed 24 Hen. VIII. c. 13. and see 1 Jac. I. c. 25. § 45.

Dukes and Marquisses may wear in their Doublets and Sleeveless Coats Cloth of Gold of Tissue, not exceeding the Yard, but in none other of their Garments. - Ib.

Viscounts, the Prior of St. John of Jerusalem within the Realm, and Barons, may wear in their Doublets or Sleeveless Coats, Cloth of Gold,

Silver, and Tinsel. - Ib.

Appeal against the Principal and Accessary. -

None to be outlawed upon Appeal of Commandment, Force, Aid, or Receipt, until he that is appealed of the Deed be attainted.

Proviso for Appeal at the next County against Accessaries as well as Principals. -

For the Punishment of malicious Appeals. -

Appellor for a false Appeal shall suffer a Year’s Imprisonment, and shall also restore to the Parties appealed their Damages, and if Appellor cannot pay them. Inquiry shall be made of Abbettors of Appeals, and they shall be punished by Imprisonment and Damages, and there shall be no Essoin for the Appellor.

To whom and in what Cases, Commissions of Oyer and Terminer shall be granted. - -

A Writ to hear and determine Appeals before Justices assigned shall not be granted but in a special Case, and for a Cause certain, when the King commandeth. When the Parties appealed or indicted be kept long in Prison, they shall have a Writ of Odio & Alia. -For Persons appealed.

Of bringing Persons appealed by the Appealors. - -

See 8 Hen. VI,. c. 10.—10 Hen. VI. c.6.

Of letting to Mainprize Persons appealed. *

Appeals of Felonies shall not be abated, wherever the Appellors make mention, within Appeals,of the Day and the Hour and the Place, and with what Weapon the Death was inflicted, and of what Manner of Goods the Robbery was.

Against the Diminution of the Possessions of Archbishopricks and Bishopricks, and for avoiding of Dilapidations of the same.

Recital that all the Archbishopricks and Bishopricks within this Realm of England, were in Ancient Times founded by his Majesty’s most Noble Progenitors, Kings of this Realm, and that in respect thereof his Majesty is lawful and rightful Patron of all and every of the same, and that by Law no Archbishop or Bishop can make any Lease of his Land to a Subject for more than Twenty-one Years or Three Lives, and therefore, that for maintaining the Revenues of Bishopricks, in future; Archbishops and Bishops are declared disabled from alienating any Possessions of their Sees to the Crown, and every such Alienation declared void. -

Battail (Battle.)

Statutu de Magnis Assjs’ et Duellis.

Battle, nor the Grand Assize, may not be joined between Relations, until after the Third Degree, where they claim by the same Descent. - Stat. Temp, incert.

Battle may be joined between Brothers where One is a Feoffee, and the other claims byDescentof Inheritance. Ib.

Battle is joined, and the Grand Assize not, where _one is enfeoffed, and vouches to warranty, under the Charter which he hath of his Feoffee.

The Vouchee may deny the Charter by the Body of One of his Freemen ; and there the Grand Assize lieth not, but Battle. - Ib.

The Grand Assize is joined, and Battle not, where a Man selleth Land to another by Charter, and such Purchaser selleth over the Land, and hath no more Land, whereby he gives up the Charter by which he was first enfeoffed. Then cometh the Heir of the First Feoffee, and impleadeth him by Writ of Right; he cannot defend his Seisin by the Body of One of his Freemen, but must put himself on God and the Grand Assize. - Ib.

Benefice#.

Of Provisoes of Ecclesiastical

Benefices. - - - 25 Edw. III. St. 4.

Recital of Proceedings in the Parliament of Carlisle, Stat. 35 Edw. I.; and that the Holy Church of England was founded in the Estate of Prelacy, within the Realm of England, by the King’s Progenitors, to inform them and the People of the Law of God„ and to do Hospitalities, Labours, and other Works of Charity; and that the King and others, Earls, Barons,

&c. had and ought to have the Custody and Presentations of Benefices. Ib.

That the Pope bestowed Benefices (accroaching to him the Seigniory thereof,) on Aliens who would never dwell in England, and on Cardinals who could not dwell there, although he was not of Right, by the Law of England, the Patron or Advower thereof; and that great Evil would ensue if such things should be suffered. - Ib.

That although, in the said Parliament of Carlisle, Provision was made against such Evil, yet that the Pope continued to give such Benefices, and reserved the First Fruits to himself. lb.

Collations and Presentations to Benefices to be free. - Ib.

Where the Pope maketh Provision to a Dignity or Benefice of the Church of the King’s Avowry, the King shall for that Time present, as before free Election was granted. - Ib.

So, in cases of Provision to Religious Houses, and Benefices of the Advowsons of the Clergy. - Ib.

Saving Right of Presentation to Parties presenting, or where not Provision made by the Pope. - Ib.

Presentations of Patrons shall, on Failure, lapse to the King. - Ib.

Of every Person that goeth begging, and is able to serve or labour, it shall be done of him as of him that departed out of the Realm, and other Places aforesaid, without Letter Testimonials ; and that Beggars impotent to serve shall abide in the Towns where they dwell; and if the Towns cannot find them, then the said Beggars shall draw them to other Towns.

See 12 Ric. II. c. 3.

For taking away the Benefit of Clergy from certain Felonious Offenders. -

Recital that a certain Kind of evil-disposed Persons, commonly called Cutpurses or Pickpurses, but indeed by the Laws of this Land very Felons and Thieves, do confeder together, making among themselves as it were a Brotherhood or Fraternity of an Art or Mystery, to live idly by the secret Spoil of the good and true Subjects of this Realm, and as well at Sermons and preaching of the Word of God, and in Places and Time of doing Service and Common Prayer in Churches, Chapels, Closets, and Oratories, and not only there, but also in the Prince’s Palace House, yea and Presence, and at the Places and Courts of Justice, and at the Times of Ministration of the Laws in the same, and in Fairs, Markets, and other Assemblies of People, yea and at the Time of doing of Execution of such as have been attainted of any Murder, Felony, or other criminal Cause, ordained chiefly for Terror and Example of Evil Doers, do, without respect or regard of any Time, Place, or Person, or any Fear or Dread of God, or any Law or Punishment, under the Cloak of Honesty, by their outward Apparel, Countenance, and Behaviour, subtilty, privily, craftily, and feloniously take the Goods of divers good and honest Subjects from their Persons, by cutting and picking their Purses, and other felonious Slights and Devices, to the utter undoing and Impoverishment of many.

Offenders convicted, &c. of stealing privily from the Person, shall not have Benefit of Clergy.

Statute

For the Uniformity of Service, and Administration of Sacraments, throughout the Kealm.

Recital, that various Forms of Common Prayer are used in England and Wales; and that the Book of Common Prayer, after the Use of the Church of England, had been prepared by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Bishops, &c. under the King’s Appointment; and of the Approbation thereof by the Lords and Commons in Parliament.

Former Offences, in using various Forms of Prayer, pardoned. - -

All Ministers shall celebrate Divine Service, 8tc. according to the said Book of Common Prayer.

Ministers refusing to use the said Book of Common Prayer, or wilfully using any other Form of open Prayer or Preaching, &c. in Derogation of the said Book—Penalty, First Offence, Loss of Profits of One Benefice for a Year and Six Months Imprisonment. - - -

Second Offence, One Year’s Imprisonment, and Deprivation of all Benefices. -

Third Offence, Imprisonment for Life. -

Persons not beneficed, Six Months Imprisonment.

Second Offence, Imprisonment for Life. - -

Persons, byPlays, Songs, or Words, depraving or despising the said Book, or compelling or procuring the Use of any other Form, or interrupting any Minister using the same—Penalty, First Offence, j^io.

Second Offence, £20.

Third Offence, Forfeiture of Goods, and Imprisonment for Life.

On default of Payment of Penalty on First Offence, Three Months Im -prisonment. -

Second Offence, Six Months Imprisonment. -

Justices of Oyer and Terminer may hear and determine Offences.

Archbishops and Bishops may join such Justices of Oyer and Assize. -

Prayers in Latin, 8cc. may be read by learned Persons, and in the Universities. -

Except Mass.

Psalms or Prayers from the Bible allowed. - - -

For the perpetual Maintenance of Rochester Bridge.

Two Wardens and Twelve Assistants shall be chosen yearly, after Easter, by the Commonalty of the Lands contributory to Rochester Bridge, to manage and account for the Revenues belonging to the said Bridge, &c. -

Wardens neglecting to give Notice of Election, &c.—Penalty ^5.

Wardens elected refusing to become bound — Penalty ^10, to the Use of the said Bridge.

Leases of Lands shall be signed by both Wardens and the Majority of the Assistants, and shall be registered, &c.

Such Leases shall be made as required by Tenants in Tail under Stat. 32 Hen. VIII. c. 28.

Saving for Houses not having above Three Acres of Land, 8cc.

Leases shall not be made for Fines.

Covenants therein.

Present Tenants shall be preferred.

Tenants going out shall have Re-compence for Improvements.

The Wardens alone may sue as under Stat. 9 Hen. V. St. 1. c. 12. -

Owners of Lands, formerly contributory to repair of the Bridge, shall be taxed only in default of the Revenues of the Bridge.

For the punishing and correcting of Deceits and Frauds committed by Sorters, Combers, and Spinsters of Wool, and Weavers of Woollen Yarn.

Recital of Frauds on Clothiers, &tc. by Sorters, &c. of Wool.

Such Sorters, &c. purloining or embezzling Wool or Yarn delivered to them by Clothiers and the Receivers thereof, shall, for the First Offence, recompense the Party grieved, or be whipped and set in the Stocks, as shall be limited by Justices of Peace or Chief Officers.

Second Offence, the like or such further Punishment by whipping, or put in the Stocks, as the said Justices, &c. shall see fit.

Receivers punishable as Principals. Like Punishment on Spinners of Wool, in the Towns of Cogshall, Bocking, Braintree, Hallsteed, Wit-ham, and Colchester, in Essex, delivering short Reels of Yarn, the said Reel containing about Two Yards. -

Marshal, &c. taking Reward to connive at Prisoner’s Escape — Penalty ^500, Loss of Office, and Incapacity.

Proviso for Securities given for Lodging within the Rules of the said Prison. -

Such Note sufficient Evidence of Person being a Prisoner.

An Act of Recognition of the Queen's Highness’s Title to the Imperial Crown of this Realm. -The Recognition and the Limitation of the Crown under Stat. 35Hen. VHI. c. I. declared perpetual; and all Sentences, &c. to the contrary declared void. -

For Provision to be made for the Surety of the Queen’s Majesty’s most Royal Person, and the Continuance of the Realm in Peace.

In Cases of Invasion or Rebellion by or for any Person pretending Title to the Crown, all such Persons, by Judgment of Commissioners to be appointed for that Purpose, shall, on Proclamation, be excluded and disabled from all Claim to the Crown; and may, with their Abettors, &c. be pursued to Death by all Subjects.

And in case of the Queen’s Death, the Party causing the same shall be excluded, and pursued to Death.

In case of the violent Death of the Queen, the Privy Council, 8tc. shall, on Examination, proclaim the guilty Parties, and use Force in pursuing them to Death ; and all who resist the Execution of this Law shall be excluded from the Crown.

All Subjects shall assist the Privy Council, and shall not be therefore impeached in Body, Lands, or Goods.

Associations in Defence of Her Majesty’s Person and Title declared consonant to this present Act.

§ 9-

An Act against Merchants carrying of Goods from one Port to another without a Certificate from the Customer. - - - 3 Hen. FII. c. 7. (8.)

If Goods be brought into one Port and customed, and then removed into another, a Certificate thereof shall be produced at the latter Port.

Customers giving improper Certificate shall lose their Office, and make Fine to the King at his Pleasure.

Forfeiture of Goods, if discharged or put to Sale, before the Certificate delivered. - - -

Merchandizes shall be entered in the Customers’ Books in the Name of the true Owner.

A Common Officer in a City or Town shall not be Customer, Comptroller, or Searcher.

Reasons for passing this Act.

Cities of York, Exeter, Bristol, Chester, and Norwich, appointed for assaying, 8cc. Wrought Plate. -Goldsmiths, &c. in the said Cities incorporated a Company.

His Allowance and Oath. - -Diet Box to be locked with Three Locks. - -

May be annually conveyed to the Mint in the Tower.

This Act appears to be superseded by the Stat. 4 Hen. VII. c. 24.;

These Provisions are repealed by the Effect of Hen. Vll. c. 24., which declares the Fine valid to conclude Privies and Strangers, £f?r. upon the Proclamations required being made in the Court of Common Pleas. The Stat. 4 Hen. Vll. c. 24. also contains a Saving of Action against Parties to the Fine, having no Title without Limitation of Time ; no such Saving is in this Act of I Ric. III.

See the Stats. 1 Mar. Stat. 2. c. 7. and 31 Eliz. c. 2., which refer only to the Stat. 4 Hen. VII. without noticing this Act.

The Statute of Herring. -

JFW&*

Herrings shall not be forestalled at Sea. -

STAT.3iEdw.III. St.2. C.2. EXTENDED to all Towns where Herring is taken. -

Lord Chancellor and Lord Treasurer shall REGULATE the BUYING and selling of Fish and Wines. -The Provisions of these Acts may be considered as entirely superseded by modern Statutes, particularly 23 Geo. II. c. 24. and many subsequent Acts relating to the British Fisheries. The Act was intended to prevent forestalling and undue dealing in the Fair of Great Yarmouth, for which Purpose it was enacted, by c. I. ante, u That no Herrings should be bought or sold in the Sea, till the Fisheries were come into the Haven, and the Cable of the Ship drawn to Land " and c. 2. ante, regulated the Order and Time of selling Herrings, and the Price thereof: it also directed that the Hundred of Herrings should be Six Score, and the Last Ten Thousand. The Superintendance of the Fair was vested in the Barons of the Cinque Ports. By cap. 3. Power was given to the Chancellor, Treasurer, and Council to regulate the Sale of Stock Fish of Saint Botolph, and Salmon of Berwick, and of fVines and Fish at Bristol, and elsewhere.

See Jparmout!) (great).

The Statute of Herring. - -1

Recital of Stat.31 Edw. III. c.l, 2. and the Inconveniences arising from the same. -

All Persons may buy Herrings openly, but not privily. -

No Man to interrupt another in a Bargain of Herring, nor bid upon him —Penalty, Double his Proffer to the Crown. - - -

Fishermen may sell their Herrings as soon as they arrive.

See Notes to 31 Edw. III. St. 2. c.3.

Concerning sowing of Flax and Hemp.

Every Person occupying Land apt for Tillage shall for every Sixty Acres sow yearly one Quarter of an Acre of Flax or Hemp Seed — Penalty 3s. 4d.

Limitation of Suits for Penalties,

One Year; and Presentment for the King, Two Years.

Any Person taking Eggs of Hawks or Swans—Imprisonment, a Year and a Day, and Fine at the King’s Will;

One Moiety to the Crown, and the other to the Owner of Grounds where Eggs taken. - - -

None shall bear any Hawk of the Breed of England, called Nyesse,

Gossehawk, Tassel, Laner, Lanerette, or Falcon, upon Forfeiture of his Hawk to the King, and the said Hawk to be at the King’s Pleasure; and that all Persons that bring any Nyesse, Hawk or Hawks, from beyond Sea, bring a Certificate, under the Customer’s Seal, of the Port where he first landed -, or, if he come from Scotland, then under the Seal of the Warden, or his Lieutenant, of that March that he comes through, testifying that the same Hawk or Hawks be of the Parties beyond Sea, or of Scotland, upon the same Pain.

Persons bringing any such Hawk to the King, shall have a reasonable Reward of the King, or else the same Hawk.

Archbishops and Dukes shall maintain Seven stoned trotting Horses for the Saddle, of the Age of Three Years and upwards, 14 Hands high—Penalty ^>20 every Three Months for each Horse; One Moiety of Penalty to the Crown, and the other to Party suing. 33 Hen. VIII. c.$. § 1.

Marquisses, Earls, and Bishops, the early Value of whose Bishoprick is of the yearly Value of aThousand Pounds

or above, shall maintain Five stoned trotting Horses for the Saddle, of the Age and Height aforesaid, upon the Pain above specified.

Every other Bishop, Viscount, and Baron, having Lands, Tenements,

Fees, Annuities, or Offices for Term of his Life to the clear yearly Value of a Thousand Marks or above, shall maintain Three stoned trotting Horses for the Saddle, of the Age and Height afore-mentioned, upon the Pain above specified. - "

Every other Bishop, Viscount, and Baron, and also every Spiritual Person having Benefices or Promotions to the yearly Value of Five hundred Marks, and every Temporal Person having Lands, Tenements, Offices, Fees, or Annuities for Term of his Life, in his own Right or his Wife's, to the yearly Value of Six hundred Marks, shall maintain Two stoned trotting Horses for the Saddle, in manner and form and upon the Pain afore rehearsed. -

Every other Spiritual Person under the Degree of a Bishop, having Benefices or Promotions to the clear yearly Value of One hundred Pounds or above, and not to the yearly Value of Five hundred Marks, and every other Person temporal not afore-mentioned, whose Wife shall wear any Gown of Silk, or any French Hood or Bonnet of Velvet, with any Habiliment, Paste, or Egg of Gold, Pearl, or Stone, or any Chain of Gold about their Necks, or in their Partlets, or in any Apparel of their Body, shall maintain One stoned trotting Horse for the Saddle —Penalty ^10 every Three Months;

One Moiety to the Crown, and the other to Party suing.

Recital of the Evils arising from Waste of Houses, and converting tilled Land into Pasture.

Owners of Houses let to farm with Twenty Acres of Land, shall maintain Houses and Buildings thereon necessary for Tillage.

On their Default, the King, or other Lord of the Fee, shall receive Half the Profits, and apply the same in repairing such Houses, but shall not gain thereby any Freehold, but only Power to take, receive, and have the Issues and Profits.

For approving the Opinions of certain Judges concerning the Statute and Commission io Ric. II., and for repealing all Proceedings in the Parliament of ii Ric.II. - 21 Ric.II. c. 12.

Recital, that Questions put to the Judges, An. 11 Ric. II. respecting the Statute 10 Ric. II. and the Commission then made, as follow :— - Ib.

1. If the same Statute be derogatory to the King’s Prerogative ? - Ib.

2. How the Procurers and Advisers of the same were punishable ? Ib.

3. How they ought to be punished that did interrupt the King, so that he might not exercise those Things that pertaineth to his Prerogative ?

And that of one Assent it was answered, that they ought to be punished as Traitors. - Ib.

4. Whether the Parliament can

proceed on other Business than that limited by the King ? And that of one Mind they answered, that the King in this Party shall have the Rule; and if any do contrary, he ought to be punished as a Traitor. - Ib.

5. Whether the King, whensoever • it pleascih him, might dissolve the

Parliament ? And that it was of one Mind answered, that he may ; and if

any would proceed In the Parliament against the King’s Will, he is to be punished as a Traitor. - -21 Ric, II. c, 12.

6. Whether the Lords and Com-

mons might, without the King’s Will, impeach Offenders upon their Offences in the Parliament ? And that it was by one Mind answered, that they might not; and he that doth contrary is to be punished as a Traitor. - -16,

7. How he is to be punished that moved in the Parliament for Production of the Record of the Deposition of King Edward II. ? And that of one Accord they answered, that as well he that so moved, as the other which by force of the same Motion brought the said Statute into the Parliament House, be as Traitors worthy

to be punished. - - 16,

8. Whether the Judgment against the Earl of Suffolk in 10 Ric. II. were erroneous and revocable ? And that of one Assent they said, that if the same Judgment were now to be given, the same Justices and Serjeant aforesaid would not give the same, because it seemed to them that the same Judgment is revocable as erroneous in every Part* and that in witness thereof the Justices and Serjeant aforesaid to this Present did set

their Seals. 16,

And that it was demanded of all the States of the Parliament, how they thought of the Answers aforesaid ; and they said, that they thought that the said Justices made and gave their Answers duly and lawfully, as good and lawful liege People of the King ought to do ; and in the same Manner, Sir Thomas of Skelton, learned in the Law, and William Hankeford and William Brenchley, the King’s Serjeants, demanded by the King of their Advice in this Behalf, said that the Answers were good and lawful} and that they would hare given the same Answers, if the said Questions had been demanded of them. And my Lord William Thir-ning, Chief Justice of the Common Bench, said that the Declaration of Treason not declared belongcth to the Parliament; but if he were a Lord, or a Peer of the Parliament, if he had been demanded, he would have said in the same Manner; and in like Manner said my Lord William Rikehyll, Justice of the Common Place; and after the coming of my Lord Walter Clopton, Chief Justice, he said in likewise: and that therefore the said Answers should be adjudged and affirmed for good and sufficient in the said Parliament. - 16.

The Proceedings in Parliament II Ric. II. repealed, and the Parties restored to their Lands. - - 16.

For the King’s Tenants going in his

Wars. - 14Edw.IV. c.i.

All Persons who shall go with the King, in his Service, into France, shall have Licence to enter, and have Livery of Lands descended to them, and holden of the King without Fine; and such Persons shall have Licences to make Feoffments to the Use of their Wills. - Ib.

If such Persons die abroad, their Heirs being within Age, their Feoffees shall have their Estates, though the Feoffment was by Collusion, or otherwise intituling the King; except as to Lands of the King’s own Grant. - Ib.

The King’s Grantees may grant for the Duration of their own Interests. - Ib.

Feoffees of Persons dying, holding by Knights’ Service, shall have the Ward and Marriage of their Heir,

and of their Lands. - Ib.

Saving as to personal Service. - Ib.

The Council shall determine Disputes as to this Act. - Ib.

In eschewing Diversities of Opinion upon judicial Acts, and Exemplifications of the same made or had in the Time or Times of Henry the Fourth,

Henry the Fifth his Son, and Henry the Sixth his Son, or any of them, late Kings of England successively, in Deed and not of Right, it is enacted, that all Fines and final Concords levied or made of any Lands, and all judicial Acts, Recoveries, and Processes, other than by Authority of any Parliament holden in any of their Times, and Exemplifications thereof, shall be of like Force as if the said Acts were commenced, sued, had or determined in the Time of any King lawfully reigning in this Realm, and obtaining the Crown of the same by just Title. - § 1.

So, in respect of Creations of Nobility, except to Rebels or Enemies. - § 2.

So, in respect of Liberties, Divisions of Counties, Grants of Incorporation, &c. to any Bodies Corporate. § 3.

So, in respect of Licences or Pardons of Alienation, or to enter into Lands descended, without Livery; and of Licences to found any Spiritual House, &c. or any Fraternity, Guild,

&c. or to give or receive any Lands ; and of Licences of Appropriation, or to make Elections; and of Pardons to Corporations, for Purchases; and of Liveries or Restitutions of Temporal-ties to Spiritual Persons. - § 4.

So, in respect of Letters Patent of the said late pretensed Kings founding of religious Houses, as to die Corporations and Sites of the same. - Ib.

So, in respect of Assignments of Dower made by any of the said late pretensed Kings. - § 5.

Proviso for the King and the Duchess of Bedford ; and of Lands assured in Mortmain, by any of the said late pretensed Kings, which were given to them to that Intent. - §§5,6.

Lollards.

For repressing of Heresies and Punishment of Heretics.

The Orthodoxy of the Church of England asserted. - -

Recital, that a new Sect do perversely preach and teach divers new Doctrines, and wicked and heretical Opinions. - - - -

None shall preach without Licence from his Diocesan, or preach or write against the Faith of Holy Church *, ot hold Schools for teaching, or favour the Teachers of the new Doctrines. -

Heterodox Books shall be delivered up to the Diocesan. -

The Diocesan may arrest and imprison Offenders till they purge themselves or abjure their heretical Opinions. - - - -

So that the said Diocesan, by himself or his Commissaries, proceed against such Persons to all Effect of the Law, and determine the same, according to the canonical Decrees, within Three Months after the said Arrest. - -

For the Suppression of Heresy and Lollardy.

Recital, that Evils had arisen from the religious Sect called Lollards.

The Lord Chancellor, Lord Treasurer, Judges, Justices of Peace, and other Officers, shall be sworn against Lollardy; and assist the Ordinaries and Commissaries in arresting Lollards. -

In regard of Offenders, the King shall have all the Lands and Tenements which the said Convicts have in Fee Simple, and holden of him immediately, as forfeit; and that the other Lords, of whom the Lands and Tenements of such Convicts be holden, immediately after that the King is so seised and answered of the Year, the Day, and the Waste, have Livery out of the King's Hands of the Lands and Tenements aforesaid of them so holden, as the Case of Attainder of Felony; except the Lands and Tenements which be holden of the Ordinaries or their Commissaries, which entirely shall remain to the King as forfeit; and moreover, that all the Goods and Chattels of these Persons so convicted be forfeit to our Sovereign Lord the King. -

Justices of the King’s Bench, &c. shall inquire of Heretics, as Lollards.

Capias against them.

Cognizance of Heresy belongs to the Spiritual Judges.

Heretics indicted may be bailed. -

Every Ordinary shall have sufficient Commissaries orCommissary dwelling in every County. -

Qualification of Jurors impan-ncllcd. -

If Persons arrested break Prison, the Goods and Chattels which he had the Day of such Arrest shall be forfeited to the King, and his Lands, &c. which he had the same Day, seized also in the King’s Hands, the King shall have the Profits thereof from the said Day, until he yield to the Prison from which he escaped.

Justices may inquire of such Escapes. -

Statute

For regulating the making of Worsteds in Norwich and Norfolk.

Recital of the Deceits practised in making Worsteds in Norwich and Norfolk.

Worsted Weavers every Year shall choose Four Wardens in Norwich, and other Four in Norfolk, who shall be sworn before the Mayor of the City and Steward of the Duchy of Lancaster. -

Power of the said Wardens to survey Worsteds, and to punish Offenders.

The Length and Breadth of Pieces of Worsted Cloths.

Wardens may seize defective Cloths. -

The Mayor, Steward, &c., may inquire of, hear and determine Offences. -

The said Mayor or Steward, and Twelve Artificers, shall inquire of the Eight Wardens.

Wardens, if defective in their Duties or Work—Punishment.

Wardens may search in Norwich,

Norfolk, Suffolk, and Cambridge.

Defective Goods forfeited.

One Moiety to Mayor, &c., and the other to Wardens.

Every Man of the said Craft shall set his proper Mark upon his Worsteds. -

Certain Days and Places shall be assigned by the said Wardens for their Search. -

Wardens shall set their Mark to Worsteds properly made, and correct such as are defective.

Worsteds sold, not marked, the first Seller thereof shall forfeit to the Crown the Price of the Piece so by him sold. -

All Officers shall be attendant upon the Searchers. -

For the Prevention of Inconveniences happening by the long Intermission of Parliaments.

If no Parliament summoned before the 16th of Sept, in the Third Year after the last Day of the last Sitting, then the Parliament to assemble at Westminster, in the Manner, by the Means, and at the Time hereafter mentioned. -

Lord Chancellor and Commissioners to take an Oath to issue Writs.

Failing to issue Writs — Perjury and Disability of Office, and other Punishments, at Discretion of Parliament. - -

If Writs not issued, and Parliament do not meet, Peers enabled to meet in the Old Palace of Westminster, and by virtue of this Act to issue Writs.

Clerks of the Petty Bag, &c. to prepare such Writs for Signature of the Lords.

Omitting so to do, Punishment at Discretion of Parliament.

Messenger, &c. to deliver Writs.

Omitting so to do, Punishment at Discretion of Parliament.

Peers to assemble the Third Monday in January. -

In case Parliament not assembled before 23d January, then to be assembled by such Means only as hereafter mentioned.

Sheriffs,and the Chancellor, Master, and Scholars of the Universities, and the Mayor and Bailiffs of Berwick, to cause Knights, &c. to be chosen as if Writs had issued.

If Default, then Electors to proceed. -

Knights, &c. elected, to appear and serve in Parliament.

Sheriffs, &c. to make Returns as if Writs had issued.

If Default, then Electors to make Returns, which shall be good.

Plymouth (Port of).

Statute

For the a mending and Maintenance of the Havens and Ports of Plymouth, Dartmouth, Teign-mouth, Falmouth, and Fowey, in the Counties of Devon and Cornwall. -Recital of the Prejudice to the said Ports by Stream Works of Tinners in the said Counties. -Tinners shall not work in Stream Works without sufficient Hatches and Ties, &c.—Penalty ^*io; One Moiety to the Crown, and the other to the Inhabitants of the said Ports, &c. suing for same. -

Penalty increased to £20 by Stat.

27 Hen. VIII. c. 23. § 2. and extended to the Labourers.

Statute

That the Appeals in such Cases as have been used to be pursued to the See of Ro^ie, shall not be from henceforth had nor used but within this Realm. - - - 24 Hen. VIII. c. 12

Recital of the Pre-eminence, Power, and Authority of the King of England. §1.

Of the Power, Learning, and Wisdom of the Body Spiritual. - Ib.

Of the Power, &c. of the Temporally. - Ib.

Of the Laws and Provisions by former Kings, Edward the First, Edward the Third, Richard the Second, and Henry the Fourth, against the Intrusions of the See of Rome. - Ib.

And of the Appeals to Rome, and the Evils thereof. - Ib.

All testamentary and matrimonial Causes, and all Suits for Tithes, Oblations, &c., shall be adjudged by the King’s Courts Spiritual and Temporal, without regard to any Process of Foreign Jurisdiction, or any Inhibition, Excommunication, or Interdict, &c. Ib.

Prelates and Clergy shall administer the Sacraments and Service of the Church, notwithstanding such Interdicts, on Penalty of One Year’s Imprisonment, and Fine at the King’s Pleasure. - Ib.

Persons procuring Process, Appeals, Sentences, from or to the See of Rome, shall incur the Penalties of Premunire, Stat. 16 Ric.II. c.5. §2.

Appeals hereafter shall be made within the Realm; that is to say, from Archdeacons to Bishops, from Bishops to Archbishops ; from Archdeacons to the Arches Court, and thence to the Archbishop. - §3-

No Appeal from Archbishops. §4.

Saving for the Prerogative of the Archbishop of Canterbury. lb.

Appeals, in Cases touching the King, shall be made to the Upper House of Convocation. Ib.

And thence to Delegates, see 2K Hen. VIII. c. iq. § 14.— 8 Eliz. c.$. Persons appealing contrary to this Act, to incur the Penalties of Premunire. - Ib.

By Statute 27 Hen. VIII. c. 15., Sections I, 2, and 7. of this Act are recited and continued for Three Years, &c. By 35 Hen. VIII. c. 16. similar Provisions were made to endure for the King’s Life, with a Clause of the same Nature, but more explicit than §7 of this Act. Stat. 3 4 Edw. VI. c. II., a

temporary Act for the like Purposes, is wholly expired. By Stat. I 2 Ph. M. c. 8. this Act -was repealed; but by 1 Eliz. c.i. § 10. it is again revived and continued in all Time from and after the last Day of that Session of Parliament.

Sail Cloth.

Against the deceitful and false making of Mildernix and Powle Davies, whereof Sail Cloths for the Navy and other Shipping are made. -

Recital that Cloth called Mildernix and Powle Davies, used for Sails of Ships, had been imported until 32 Eliz.; and of the Unskilfulness of Workmen, and Badness of such Cloth, lately made in England.

None shall make such Cloth except such as shall have been apprenticed and brought up to the Trade—Penalty 20s. for every Month.

Such Cloth shall be made only of Hemp, not less than Thirty-three Yards in Length, and not less than Three Quarters of a Yard in Breadth.

Selling such Cloth, not duly bleached, &c. — Penalty 5s. per Piece.

One Moiety of Penalties to the Crown, and the other Moiety to the Party suing for same.

Statute of Labourers. - - 23 Edw. III. c. 1.

Proclamation concerning Servants, who shall be bound to serve when required. - -

The Rate of Wages fixed as in the 20 Edw. III. *

Persons refusing to serve shall be committed to next Gaol, there to remain till they find Surety to serve. - - -

Labourers departing from their Service, to be imprisoned.

None, under the same pain, to presume to receive or to retain any such in his Service. -

The old Wages, and no more, to be given to Servants, upon pain of doubling of that to him which thereof shall feel himself aggrieved, or other suing for the same.

Lords of Towns or Manors, offending against this Ordinance, shall forfeit Treble Value. -

If any, before this present Ordinance, hath covenanted with any so to serve for more Wages, he shall not be bound by reason of the same Covenant to pay; nor, upon the said pain, shall presume any more to pay. - -

Excess of Wages received by Servants, to be refunded by them to Informer. - 25 Edw. Ill, St. 2. c.$.

Sheriffs, Constables, &c. not to take any thing of Servants for Fees. - Ib. c.6.

Justices to enquire thereof. - Ib.

Forfeitures to be applied in aid of the Subsidy for the Time being. - * lb.

Abettors of Servants offending shall be grievously punished, by the Discretion of the Justices. - lb. c. 7.

Statute

For Sheriffs to be discharged upon their Accounts, and to have Allowance for their reasonable Expbncbs, in the Court of the Exchequer. - 34&*35Hen. VIII.e.i6.

Recital, that Sheriffs of Counties were chargeable with certain ancient Farms ; that is to say, De firm’ com' post terr* dat’ (the Origin thereof);

Pro proficuo com* (the Origin thereof);

Farms of Purprestures, &c.; and that the said Farms were not fully levied, from Ignorance of the Lands or Persons liable, from being discharged by the King, or coming into his Possession on Suppression of religious Houses. § i.

The Remedy necessary for Discharge of Sheriffs. - Ib.

Sheriffs to be sworn to bring in Rolls of Account, specifying the Sums levied for the said Farms, and the Persons, Lands, &c. of or for which they were levied. - Ib.

The Court of Exchequer may make Allowances for the Excess of the Amount of Farms above the Sums actually levied. - Ib.

And may issue Process for reviving and recovering the Amount of any Matters wrongfully withholden. - Ib.

Certain Sums respited to former Sheriffs, on account of the said

Farms, &c., on their Petitions.

They that dwell at the Stews in Southwark shall not be impan-nelled in Juries, nor keep any Inn or Tavern, except there.

Recital, that divers Persons of great Poverty, without Conscience, and of an evil Governance, now and late dwelling in a Place suspected, called the Stews, in the Borough of Southwark, as well by the Receipt of common Women, Thieves, Man-killers, and Adulterers, as by Murders and privy Robberies, as well by themselves as by many others there harboured, without Pity, Loyalty, and good Conscience, there done, have suddenly come to great Riches, by which they have purchased great Livings of Lands, &c., to great yearly Values; and, because of their Sufficiency of Freehold so purchased, have been returned by the Sheriff of the said County, and other Bailiffs, in Inquests. - Ib.

For regulating the Privy Council, and for taking away the Court commonly called the Star Chamber.

Recital of Mag. Car. 9 Hen. III. c.29.—5 Edw.HI. c.9—25Edw.HI. Stat. 5. c.4. — 28 Edw. III. c.3.— 36Edw. III. 0.15.—42 Edw.III. c.3. —3Hen. VII. c. 1., and 21 Hcn.VIII. c. 20.

Recital, that all Matters examinable in the StarChamber maybe examinable and redressed by the Common Law; and that the CouncilTable has assumed a Power contrary to Law.

Court of Star Chamber and all its Powers dissolved. -

The like Jurisdiction in several other Courts repealed and taken away.

No Court or Council to have the like Jurisdiction. -

The King or his Privy Council shall have no Jurisdiction over any Man’s Estate. ..

Great Officers and others offending — First Offence, Penalty ^500; Second Offence, Penalty £1,000, to Party grieved ; Third Offence, Loss of Office, and disabled to make any Gift, Gran:, &c. -

Treble Damages to the Party grieved. -

Every Person committed contrary to this Act shall have an Habeas Corpus, upon Payment of the ordinary Fees. -

Cause of Detainer certified by Sheriff, and thereupon Court to proceed. -

Default by Judge, &c. — Treble Damages to Party grieved. -

This Act shall extend only to the Court of Star Chamber, the Courts holden before the President and Council in the Marches of Wales, and before the President and Council in the Northern Parts, the Court of the Duchy of Lancaster, the Court of Exchequer of the County Palatine of Chester, and to all Courts of like Jurisdiction to be hereafter erected*, and to the Warrants and Directions of the Council Board, and to the Commitments, Restraints, and Imprisonments of any Person by the King’s Majesty, His Heirs or Successors, in their own Person, or by the Lords and others of the Privy Council. ...

Limitation of Information, Two Years. -

Statute

Recital of the Evils of prohibited Degrees of Marriage, and that they were extended to Cases of Carnal Knowledge; and that none can dispense with God’s Laws. - 28 Hen. VIII, c.j. § 7.

Separation of Persons married as herein mentioned, to be valid. - Ib.

Persons not yet separated, shall be separated by the Sentence of the Ordinary, without any Appeal, 8cc. to Rome, or contrary to Stat.

24 Hen. VIII. c. 12. - Ib.

The King’s Issue by Queen Jane declared to be his lawful Children. - § 8.

Limitation of Descent of the Crown; that is to say, to the King’s Sons successively, and the Heirs of their Bodies. - Ib.

For default of Sons, then to the King’s legitimate Daughters successively, and the Heirs of their Bodies. Ib.

Recital, that in case of default of the King’s Issue, and of the Danger of naming a Successor to the Crown immediately, and of the Advantage of empowering the King to do so. - § 9.

On Failure of the King’s Issue, the King may limit the Descent of the Crown by Letters Patent, or by his Will, to any Person in Possession or Remainder, who shall be obeyed accordingly, whether Male or Female. - Ib.

Such Person shall succeed to the Crown as Heir, and as if specially herein named. - § 10.

If any of the King’s Heirs or Children usurp against each other, or if they, or the Persons to whom the Crown may be limited under the Powers of this Act, disturb the Descent or Limitation under this Act, they shall be deemed guilty of High Treason, and shall forfeit their Claims. § 11.

Any Person who, by Word, Writing, or Act, shall do any thing to the Peril of the King, his Heirs or Successors to the Crown, or for the Repeal, &c. of this Act, or of the King’s Dispositions by Force thereof, or to the Prejudice of his Marriage with Queen Jane, or any other lawful Wife or Wives he might hereafter marry, or of the Succession of his Issue or Successors under this Act, or of their Fame, Person, or Title, or shall judge the King’s former Marriages to be valid; or shall impugn the Divorces pronounced against such Marriages; or shall call the Children of such Marriages legitimate; or under any Pretence shall attempt, &c. to deprive the King, or his Heirs or Successors, of Title or Power; or, on being required, shall refuse to answer Interrogatories on Oath relating to this Act, shall be declared guilty of High Treason, and shall suffer Death, and forfeit all their Lands, Goods, &c. - § 12.

Cobacco,

For prohibiting the planting, setting, or sowing Tobacco in England and Ireland.

No Person, after the 1st Jan. 1660, shall set or plant any Tobacco — Penalty, Forfeiture of the Tobacco, or the Value, and 40s. for every Rod or Pole, and so on in proportion; One Moiety to the Crown, and the other to the Party suing. -

£ 1 o per Rod or Pole additional, see Stat. 15 Car. II. c. 7. § 15.

Sheriffs and other Officers may destroy Tobacco planted contrary to this Act. -

Persons resisting the Execution of this Act — Penalty ^5, divided as above, and recoverable by Distress. -If no Distress, Imprisonment for Two Months. -

Proviso for Physic Gardens of either University, and other private Gardens, so as the Quantity planted exceed not One Half Pole in any one Place or Garden. -

The Statute of Armour at Tour- c

NAMENTS. - -\

No Earl, Baron, or other Knight, who shall go to the Tournament, to have more than Three Esquires in Arms.

Every Esquire to bear a Cap of the Arms of his Lord. -

Armour at Tournaments regulated.

If any Earl or Baron, or other Knight, act against this Statute, he shall lose Horse and Harness, and abide in Prison, at the Pleasure of our Lord Sir Edward the King’s Son, and Sir Edmund his Brother, and the Earl of Gloucester, and the Earl of Lincoln.

If an Esquire, he shall lose Horse and Harness, and be imprisoned Three Years. -

If any Man cast a Knight to the Ground, except those armed for the Lord’s Service, the Knight shall have his Horse, and the Offender shall be punished as the Esquires aforesaid. -Armour of Noblemen’s Sons regulated. -

Spectators shall not be armed at Tournaments, upon such Forfeiture as in the Case of Esquires aforesaid.

If Groom or Footman be armed — imprisoned Seven Years.

Guests at Feasts—Arms of Heralds regulated. -

Statute

For regulating the granting of

Letters of Marque. - - 4 Hen. V. St.2. c.-j.

Recital of Part of Statute 2 Hen. V. c.6. respecting the breaking of Truces, and of the Inconveniences thereof. - Ib.

Upon Breach of Truce by Enemies, the King may grant Letters of Marque, upon Letters of Request, under the Privy Seal, in a due Form. - Ib.

If the Party do not make due Restitution, then the Chancellor of England shall cause to be made to such Party grieved, if he demand it, Letters of Marque under the Great Seal, in due Form. Ib.

Letters of Marque, where Truce is broken in Scotland or the Marches. - Ib.

The King shall give Power by Commission to the Wardens, as well of the East Marches as of the West, towards Scotland, and every of them, to hear Complaints, and to cause Letters of Request to be made thereupon. - Ib.

If Restitution be not made, then Letters of Marque shall be given in due Form, under the Seals of the said Wardens, or under his Seal to whom the Complaint shall be made. - Ib.

Statute 2 Hen. V. St at. i. c. 6. concerning Breakers of Truces, &c. recited. - - - - 14 Hen. VI. c. 8.

The said Statute suspended for Seven Years. - Ib.

See Stat. 20 Hen. FI. c. 11.

For regulating the Form of a Safe Conduct. - - -15 Hen. FI. c. 3.

Recital of the Abuse of Safe Conducts, under the Clause of "Vidimus." Ib.

Such Clause not to be inserted in a Safe Conduct, unless upon special Cause. - Ib.

In all Safe Conducts to be granted from henceforth to any Person or Persons, the Names of them, of the Ships and of the Masters, and the Number of the Mariners, with the Portage of the Ships, shall be expressed. - Ib.

See Stat. 18 Hen. FI. c. 8.

All Letters of Safe Conduct shall be inrolled in Chancery. - 20 Hen. FI. c. 1.

Recital of the Evils arising from the Non-inrolment of Letters of Safe Conduct. - Ib.

All such Letters to be inrolled in Chancery before being delivered, or to be void. - Ib.

Goods taken from Enemies not having Letters of Safe Conduct in-rolled, shall be lawful Prize. - Ib.

Proviso for Captors of Ships not shewing such Letters, although in-rolled. - Ib.

For enabling Her Majesty to appoint Commissioners to treat for an Union between the Kingdoms of England and Scotland.

Persons nominated by Her Majesty under the Great Seal to be Commissioners. -

The Commissioners to reduce their Proceedings into Instruments Quadru-partite, to be sealed and presented to the Queen and the Parliaments of England and Scotland, and thereupon such further Proceedings to be had as shall be fit.

No Matter to have effect until confirmed by the Parliament of England.

For the effectual securing the Kingdom of England from the apparent Dangers that may arise from several Acts lately passed in the Parliament of Scotland.

Persons to be nominated by the Queen are to be Commissioners to treat with Commissioners to be authorized by the Parliament of Scotland, concerning the Union, &c.

The Commissioners of both Kingdoms to reduce their Proceedings into Writing Quadrupartite, which are to be disposed of as herein mentioned, and thereupon further Proceedings to be had. -

No Commission to be granted until an Act in Scotland made for that Purpose. -

No Matter good till confirmed by the Parliament of England.

Natives of Scotland (Exception) to be considered as Aliens, until the Succession to the Crown of Scotland be settled as herein mentioned. -Persons, until the Settlement last mentioned, sending Arms, Horses, or Ammunition from England or Ireland to Scotland — Penalty £ 100, and Treble Value of such Horses, Arms, &c.; One Third Part to the Crown, and the other Third Part to Party suing for same.

[So in the Body of the Act.]

No great Cattle or Sheep to be brought out of Scotland into England or Ireland, on Forfeiture thereof; One Third Part to the Crown, and the other Two Third Parts thereof to the Party suing. - - -

Any Person may seize and detain such great Cattle and Sheep, and detain the same, until Proof made by Owners as herein mentioned.

English Cattle driven with such great Cattle, to be deemed Scotch Cattle.

Persons conspiring to evade Seizures or Forfeitures, and being indicted within One Year after Offence committed — Penalty £ 100, to be distributed as above.

In Action for executing Act, General Issue may be pleaded—Treble Costs.

For the Regulation of Servants,

Labourers, Beggars, and Vagabonds. - - - 12 Ric. II. c."j.

The Scholars of the Universities that go begging, are to have Letters Testimonial of their Chancellor, on the like Punishment as of him that departeth out of the Hundred, &c. without such Letters. - Ib.

This Statute to be executed by Sheriffs, Mayors, Gaolers, 8cc. - c. 9.

Concerning the Exoneration of Oxford and Cambridge from Payment of their First Fruits and Tenths. ... 17 Hen. VIII. c.42.

Recital of Stat. 26 Hen. VIII. c.3. for Payment of First Fruits and Tenths, and of the Reasons for exempting the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge, and the Colleges of Eton and Winchester, from such First Fruits and Tenths. - §1.

The said Universities and Colleges, and all Officers and Students, and all Offices, Promotions, 8cc. within them, and all Manors, Lands, See. belonging thereto, acquitted from the Payment of First Fruits and Tenths. - Ib.

Collectors shall be discharged in respect of the said Tenth remitted. - § 2.

The said Statute 26Hen. VIII. c.3. shall not prejudice the said Universities or the said Colleges. - Ib.

No Writs or other Process shall issue out of the King’s Courts for Payment of the said First Fruits or Tenths remitted. - § 3.

Each University shall maintain a Lecturer, to be called King Henry the Eighth’s Lecturer. - § 4.

The Chancellors of the Universities, and the Provost of Elton and Warden of Winchester, to cause Two Masses to be sung yearly on the 8th May and 8th October, and, after the King’s Death, Two Anniversaries to be kept of the said Days. - § 5.

The Heads of Houses and Graduates, &c. to take an Oath to observe this Statute. - Ib.

Osney and Rewley Monasteries in Oxford, and Barnewell in Cambridge, excepted from this Act, as also Benefices attached to Offices. - § 6.

Durham College, in Oxford, may take the Benefit of this Act. - § 7.

None shall be acquitted in respect of Possessions not belonging to the said Universities, &c. - § g.

Proviso for Colleges in Universities, fc. brewing their own Beert see Stat. 15 Car. II. e. II. § 20.

Statute

For the Punishment of unlawful Assemblies, and Rising of the Kino’s Subjects. - - - 3&4 Edw. VI. c.$.

If Twelve Persons or more, assembled together, attempt to kill or imprison any Privy Counsellor, or to alter the Laws, and, being commanded by the Sheriff, &c. to retire, shall remain together for One Hour, or do any thing in such Attempt, such Offence declared to be High Treason. - § i.

If Twelve Persons or more attempt to break down the Inclosure of any Park, or other Ground inclosed, or the Banks, &c. of any Fish Pond or Conduit ; or to have Common or Way in any such Park, &c.; or to destroy any Deer, Dovehouse, or Fish; or to pull down Houses or Barns, or to bum Stacks of Com, or to abate Rents of any Manors, &c., or the Prices of any Victual, Com, or Grain, and, being commanded to retire, shall remain together for One Hour, such Offence declared to be Felony without Clergy. - § 2.

Persons calling such Assemblies together by Bell, Trumpet, Outcry, or Handbills, &c., declared guilty of Felony without Clergy. - § 3.

Persons to the Number of Forty continuing assembled together for Two Hours, for committing the foregoing or any other traitorous, rebellious, or felonious Act, declared Traitors ; and also the Wives and Servants assisting them without Compulsion. - § 4.

Forfeiture of Lands and Goods on Attainder for such Treason. - § 5.

The King to have the Year and Day, and Waste, &c. - Ib.

Persons to the Number of Two, and under Twelve, assembled together, and attempting to kill any Subject, or to pull down any Inclosure,

&c., not dispersing on Proclamation, shall be subject to Imprisonment for One Year, and Fine and Ransom at the King’s Will. - §6.

Damages and Treble Costs to Parties grieved by such unlawful Acts. - Ib.

Where more than Two are assembled for any such unlawful Purpose, any Justice of Peace, Sheriff, Mayor,

&c., or Persons commissioned by the King, may assemble People to suppress such Assembly by force; and to apprehend, and, if necessary, kill the Offenders. - § 7.

Copyholders between Eighteen and Sixty Years old, being required by any Sheriff, &c., or by their immediate Lord, to serve the King in suppressing such Assemblies, refusing so to do, shall forfeit their Copyholds for their own Lives. - § 8.

Farmers, Artificers, Labourers, &c. between the said Ages, refusing so to serve, shall forfeit their Farms to the Landlords, for their Lives only. - Ib.

In what Cases the View of Land is grantable, and what not.

If one lose Land by Default.

When one, by an Exception dilatory, abateth a Writ after the View of the Land, the View shall not be granted, if he had View in the First Writs, in the Case herein mentioned. -

In a Writ of Dower, in the Case herein mentioned, the View shall not be granted to the Tenant.

In a Writ of Entre abated, because the Demandant misnamed the Entre. -

If the Demandant purchase another Writ of Entre, the Tenant shall not have a Second View. -

Where Lauds be demanded by reason of a Lease made by the Demandant or his Ancestor to the Tenant, and not to his Ancestor, View shall not be granted ; but if the Demise were made to his Ancestor, the View shall lie. -

- 2 Hen. IV. cc. 11,12.

Certain Restraints laid on wiiolly-born Welchmen.

No Welchman whole born in Wales, and having Father and Mother born in Wales, to purchase Lands and Tenements within the Towns of Chester,

Salop, Bridgnorth, Ludlow, Leominster, Hereford, Gloucester, Worcester, nor other Merchant Towns joining 10 the Marches of Wales, nor in the Suburbs of the same, upon pain of Forfeiture of the same Lands and Tenements to the Lords of whom such Lands and Tenements may be holden in chief, nor chosen Citizen or Burgess in any City, &c. - Ib.

Welchmen now being in any such City, &c., being Citizens or Burgesses, shall find Surety. - Ib.

No Welchman shall bear Armour within such City, upon pain of Forfeiture thereof, and imprisoned till they have made Fine. - Ib.

See Statute 27 Hen. VIII. c. 26.; but the present Act repealed by 21 Jac. I. c. 28. § II.

For the Preservation of Woods. - 35 Hen. VIII. c. 17.

Recital of the great Decay of Timber and Woods in England, as well for the building, &c. of Houses and Ships, as for Fuel and Firewood. - §1.

In Coppice Woods and Underwoods, felled at or under Twenty-four Years Growth, Twelve Standills or Storers of Oak shall be left on each Acre, which shall not be felled until they are Ten Inches Square, on Penalty of 3s. 4d. for each Standill not left or unduly felled. - - IE

Owner of such Woods causing the said Standills or Storers so left, to be cut down—Penalty, 3s. 4d. for every such Standill, &c. - Ib.

One Moiety of Penalties to the Crown, and the other to Party suing. Ib.

Underwoods, &c. felled at or under Fourteen Years Growth, shall be inclosed for Four Years, to preserve the Springs thereof — Penalty, 3s.4d. per Rood per Month. - § 2.

If above Fourteen and under Twenty-four Years Growth, they shall be inclosed for Six Years, on the like Penalty. - - . 35 Hen. VIII. c. 17. § 2.

Wood shall not be converted into Tillage or Pasture-Penalty, 40s. per Acre. - § 3.

Proviso for Underwoods felled within Twenty Years. - .

On felling Woods above Twenty-four Years Growth, Twelve great Trees shall be left on each Acre, to stand for Twenty Years, and the Wood shall be inclosed for Seven Years — Penalty, 6s. 8d. per Tree not left or unduly felled. - § 4.

And for every Rood not inclosed—

Penalty, 3s. 4d. per Month. - Ib.

Standills and Trees may be felled for build ing Sh ips,for repairingHouses,

Fences, &c. of the Owners. - § 3.

Owners of Woods, in which others have Common of Pasture, not to fell the same, except for private Use, until One Fourth Part be inclosed in severalty, cither by Agreement with the Commoners, or by the Award of Two Justices with the Consent of the Owner of the Wood and of Twelve Commoners i or, on Failure of such Consent, then at the Discretion of the Justices. - § 6.

Owners shall inclose within Three Months after the Order of Justices, and may then fell the Wood there. - Ib.

Standills and Trees shall be left on the felling Woods in such Ground so inclosed, as in other Cases. - § 7.

Wood so felled shall be inclosed for Seven Years, and the Standills and Trees kept standing, as in other Cases. Ib.

Commoners shall not put in their Beasts during such Seven Years —

Penalty, 4d. for every Beast. - § 7.

Owners of Woods unduly cutting Trees—Penalty, 6s. 8d. for every Tree. - Ib.

Penalties to be divided as in Sect. 1. ante. - Ib.

Commoners shall have Common of Pasture in the Residue of the Woods not inclosed, but during the Seven Years the Owner of the Wood shall not have Common of Pasture there. - § 8.

After the Seven Years, until the next felling, all the Commoners shall re-enjoy their Right of Common. - Ib.

Proviso for Underwoods heretofore usually inclosed. - § 9*

Until the Wood is felled in such Fourth Part so inclosed. Commoners shall continue to enjoy their Right of Common. - § 10.

This Act not to extend to Woods, exceptcommon Woods, in the Wealds of Kent, Surrey, and Sussex. - § 11.

Cui in Vita for a Wife — Receipt of a Wife, or of One in Reversion to defend. - -

A Writ of Cui in Vita granted for the Wife, where her deceased Husband lost by Default — Proceedings thereon. -

And if the Husband absent himself, and will not defend his Wife’s Rights, or against his Wife's Consent will render the Land, the Wife shall be reserved her Right. -

So the Reversion shall be reserved likewise, if Tenant in Dower, Tenant by the Law of the Land, or otherwise, for Term of Life, or by Gift, where the Reversion is reserved, do make Default or will give up.

Where the Husband, being impleaded for Land, giveth up the Land demanded untohis Adversary by Covin, and where the Husband loseth the Land in demand by Default, if the Wife, after the Death of her Husband, demandeth her Dower, the Woman demanding her Dower shall be heard. Proceedings thereon.

Statute

Recital of the Agreement between the King and the Archbishop of York, to exchange the Manors of Brighton,

Santon, Beckhay, See. in Yorkshire, belonging to the Crown, for York House,

&c. in St. Martin’s in the Fields, belonging to the Archbishoprick. - 21 Jac. I. c.30. § I.

York House, and all other the Messuages and Tenements whereof the said Archbishop is seised in Fee Simple in Right of his said Archbishoprick, situate and being in the said Parish of Saint Martin’s in the Fields, in the County of Middlesex, with the Appurtenances, assured to the King,

His Heirs, Successors, and Assigns, accordingly. lb.

The Manors of Brighton, Sandon, and Beckhay, &c. assured to the Archbishop of York and his Successors, to be holden of the Crown in Frankal-moigne. - § 2.

Leases made by the said Archbishop shall be only for Eleven Years in Possession. - § 3.

Saving for Titles in the said Manors, other than to the Crown, and the Heirs of the Earl of Lennox and Margaret his Wife, deceased, the Heirs of Edward Duke of Somerset, and the Heirs of Sir James Strang-

ways, Knight. - § 4.

Saving for Titles in York House, other than the said Toby Lord Archbishop of York, and his Successors. § 5.

The said Archbishoprick shall not be charged with additional First Fruits for the said Manors. - § 6.

During the Vacancy of the Archbishoprick, the Dean and Chapter shall enjoy the said Manors, but not York House, nor any of the Premises assured to the Crown. - § 7.
